newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn crop seen in better shape than year ago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn crop seen in better shape than year ago.

text.p: The first look at the condition of the 1997 U.S. corn crop showed it to be in better shape than last year, as of June 1, according to weekly crop reports issued by state agricultural statistics services and the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Eight percent of U.S. corn was rated excellent while 52 percent was rated good, 33 percent fair and six percent was rated poor, USDA said. One percent was rated very poor.
IOWA - Corn was rated six percent excellent, 51 percent good, 37 percent fair and six percent poor.

Reporters in the north central, northeast, southwest and southeast districts noted replanting was occurring amid cool, wet conditions. Temperatures for the week as a whole averaged six to nine degrees below normal. A warm weekend has, however, renewed optimism for the near future.
Corn planting was basically complete with 87 percent emerged, ahead of a five-year average of 76 percent.
ILLINOIS - Corn was rated 10 percent excellent, 58 percent good, 30 percent fair and two percent poor.

Fieldwork was slowed by showers but the latest rainfall had most reporters optimistic about the crop outlook although the general consensus was that warm weather was needed for crops to make good progress.
Corn planting was 100 percent complete and the crop had an average height of six inches, above a five-year average of four inches.
NEBRASKA - Corn was rated 14 percent excellent, 62 percent good, 22 percent fair and two percent poor.
Planting was 99 percent complete and 90 percent of the crop had emerged, ahead of a five-year average of 74 percent.
Reports from eastern counties indicated the presence of cutworms in some fields.
MINNESOTA - Corn was rated five percent excellent, 47 percent good, 38 percent fair, nine percent poor and one percent very poor.
Planting was 99 percent complete and 80 percent emerged, versus five-year averages of 93 and 73 percent, respectively.
May ended with several days of above-normal temperatures which warmed soils rapidly.
"Seeds that had sat in a dry, cold soil got a chance to germinate, and plants already up were able to grow taller and greener," the state's report said.
INDIANA - Corn was rated six percent excellent, 48 good, 39 percent fair, six poor and one percent very poor.
Planting was 98 percent complete, ahead of an average of 83 percent. Emergence and growth remained slow, however, due to below normal temperatures and a lack of sunshine.
